title: Run your software releases and testing with Slack bots
summary: A developer set up two Grok Slack bots that notify contributors, run builds, send 10+ agents to test like users, and hand bugs to a fixing bot.
agent_role: The release bot messages contributors, runs and monitors the build, and launches testing agents; the engineer bot triages and fixes high-priority bugs. The human starts each release and decides whether fixes go into a patch or the next release.
outcome: Author says the release and testing process is now automated.
what_they_did: A developer made two team bots with Grok Bot in a dedicated Slack channel. When told to start a release, the release bot messages each contributor about their changes so they can raise blockers. It runs the build and launches 10+ testing agents, some following a feature map and some clicking randomly. Found bugs go to an engineer bot that fixes them in Cursor.
how_it_went: The author says the whole release and testing process is now handled by the bots. He decides by severity whether a fix ships as a patch or waits for the next release.
worth_knowing: Mixing directed testers with a few random-clicking 'chaos' agents helps catch problems scripted tests miss.
prompt: When I say 'start release' in [Slack channel], list all changes merged since the last release of [repo URL] and message each contributor with links to their changes, asking for blockers. Then start the build and monitor it. Once it passes, test the build like a real user, following [feature list], plus some random exploring. Report each problem with steps to reproduce and severity. Draft fixes for high-priority issues but wait for my approval before merging or publishing any release.

curation.rationale: Detailed, original multi-agent release and testing workflow with clear roles for each bot and the human, though no numbers on results.
